# Purpose

This notebook performs the primary 2022 MiniSpin yarn-quality analysis for the
qFL-Chr.25 end-use evaluation.

The statistical strategy follows the experimental structure:

1. formal qFL-Chr.25 inference is restricted to the 16 NIILs
   (8 QTL-positive / QTL-negative sister-line pairs; 64 field samples);
2. the field sample / microginned lint lot is the biological experimental unit;
3. sample-level yarn averages are the primary response data;
4. NIL pairing is preserved using a random intercept for `pair_id`;
5. field replication is included as a fixed blocking term;
6. `Background × QTL status` is tested because the breeding value of the
   introgression may depend on genetic background;
7. actual yarn count and ratch are treated as **sensitivity variables**, not
   automatic primary covariates, because both are closely tied to the spinning
   process and ratch was selected partly from fiber length;
8. package-level observations are used as confirmation analyses;
9. individual tensile breaks are treated as technical-replicate QC data rather
   than independent biological replicates;
10. false-discovery-rate adjustment is applied across related yarn traits.

Primary yarn outcomes:

- normalized skein strength (`skein_mn_tex`);
- single-end tenacity (`yarn_tenacity_cn_tex`);
- single-end elongation (`yarn_elongation_pct`);
- yarn evenness CV (`yarn_evenness_cv_pct`);
- thin places at -50% (`yarn_thin_50`);
- thick places at +50% (`yarn_thick_50`);
- neps at +200% (`yarn_neps_200`);
- yarn hairiness (`yarn_hairiness`).

Processing outcomes analyzed separately:

- actual yarn count (`actual_yarn_count_ne`);
- card waste (`card_waste_pct`).

# 6. Prepare factors and formal NIIL analysis population

Parents and checks are retained for descriptive summaries and plotting but are not
used to define the formal qFL-Chr.25 test.

```{r prepare-analysis-data}
prepare_yarn_factors <- function(data) {

  data |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      field_sample_id =
        factor(
          field_sample_id
        ),

      genotype =
        factor(
          genotype
        ),

      background =
        factor(
          background,
          levels = c(
            "Acala",
            "Deltapine",
            "Georgia",
            "Paymaster"
          )
        ),

      nil_set =
        factor(
          nil_set
        ),

      qtl_status =
        factor(
          qtl_status,
          levels = c(
            "Negative",
            "Positive",
            "Parent_Check"
          )
        ),

      material_type =
        factor(
          material_type
        ),

      field_rep =
        factor(
          field_rep_inferred
        ),

      ratch =
        factor(
          ratch
        ),

      pair_id =
        interaction(
          background,
          nil_set,
          drop = TRUE
        )
    )
}

yarn_sample <- prepare_yarn_factors(
  yarn_sample
)

yarn_package <- prepare_yarn_factors(
  yarn_package
)

yarn_breaks <- prepare_yarn_factors(
  yarn_breaks
)

yarn_formal <- yarn_sample |>
  dplyr::filter(
    material_type == "NIIL",
    qtl_status %in% c(
      "Negative",
      "Positive"
    )
  ) |>
  droplevels()

package_formal <- yarn_package |>
  dplyr::filter(
    material_type == "NIIL",
    qtl_status %in% c(
      "Negative",
      "Positive"
    )
  ) |>
  droplevels()

break_formal <- yarn_breaks |>
  dplyr::filter(
    material_type == "NIIL",
    qtl_status %in% c(
      "Negative",
      "Positive"
    )
  ) |>
  droplevels()
```

# 12. Primary sample-level model

For each trait:

\[
Y =
Background +
QTL +
Background \times QTL +
FieldRep +
(1 | NIL\ pair)
\]

The random pair intercept preserves the matched sister-line structure while the
`Background × QTL` term tests whether the qFL-Chr.25 effect differs among genetic
backgrounds.

```{r primary-model-function}
fit_primary_yarn_model <- function(
  trait,
  data = yarn_formal
) {

  formula_text <- paste0(
    trait,
    " ~ background * qtl_status + field_rep + (1 | pair_id)"
  )

  formula_object <- stats::as.formula(
    formula_text
  )

  model_data <- data |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(
        .data[[trait]]
      )
    ) |>
    droplevels()

  fit <- tryCatch(
    lmerTest::lmer(
      formula_object,
      data = model_data,
      REML = TRUE,
      control =
        lme4::lmerControl(
          optimizer = "bobyqa",
          optCtrl = list(
            maxfun = 100000
          )
        )
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      e
    }
  )

  list(
    trait = trait,
    n = nrow(
      model_data
    ),
    model = fit
  )
}

primary_model_results <- purrr::map(
  primary_yarn_traits,
  fit_primary_yarn_model
)

names(
  primary_model_results
) <- primary_yarn_traits
```

# 13. Primary model status and singularity

```{r primary-model-status}
primary_model_status <- purrr::map_dfr(
  primary_model_results,
  function(result) {

    if (
      inherits(
        result$model,
        "error"
      )
    ) {
      return(
        tibble::tibble(
          trait = result$trait,
          n = result$n,
          fitted = FALSE,
          singular = NA,
          message =
            conditionMessage(
              result$model
            )
        )
      )
    }

    tibble::tibble(
      trait = result$trait,
      n = result$n,
      fitted = TRUE,
      singular =
        lme4::isSingular(
          result$model,
          tol = 1e-4
        ),
      message = NA_character_
    )
  }
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    trait_label =
      unname(
        trait_labels[
          trait
        ]
      )
  )

primary_model_status
```

# 14. Type III tests for primary yarn traits

```{r primary-type3-tests}
extract_type3 <- function(
  result
) {

  if (
    inherits(
      result$model,
      "error"
    )
  ) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble()
    )
  }

  anova_table <- stats::anova(
    result$model,
    type = 3,
    ddf = "Satterthwaite"
  )

  out <- as.data.frame(
    anova_table
  ) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column(
      "effect"
    ) |>
    janitor::clean_names()

  numerator_name <- intersect(
    names(out),
    c(
      "num_df",
      "ndf"
    )
  )

  denominator_name <- intersect(
    names(out),
    c(
      "den_df",
      "ddf"
    )
  )

  f_name <- intersect(
    names(out),
    c(
      "f_value",
      "f"
    )
  )

  p_name <- intersect(
    names(out),
    c(
      "pr_f",
      "p_value"
    )
  )

  tibble::tibble(
    trait = result$trait,
    effect = out$effect,
    numerator_df =
      if (
        length(
          numerator_name
        ) > 0
      ) {
        out[[numerator_name[1]]]
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
    denominator_df =
      if (
        length(
          denominator_name
        ) > 0
      ) {
        out[[denominator_name[1]]]
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
    f_value =
      if (
        length(
          f_name
        ) > 0
      ) {
        out[[f_name[1]]]
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
    p_value =
      if (
        length(
          p_name
        ) > 0
      ) {
        out[[p_name[1]]]
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
  )
}

primary_type3_tests <- purrr::map_dfr(
  primary_model_results,
  extract_type3
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    trait_label =
      unname(
        trait_labels[
          trait
        ]
      )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    effect
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fdr_p =
      stats::p.adjust(
        p_value,
        method = "BH"
      )
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

primary_type3_tests
```

# 16. Estimated marginal means by QTL status

```{r qtl-emmeans}
extract_qtl_emmeans <- function(
  result
) {

  if (
    inherits(
      result$model,
      "error"
    )
  ) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble()
    )
  }

  em <- emmeans::emmeans(
    result$model,
    ~ qtl_status
  )

  as.data.frame(
    em
  ) |>
    janitor::clean_names() |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      trait = result$trait,
      .before = 1
    )
}

primary_qtl_emmeans <- purrr::map_dfr(
  primary_model_results,
  extract_qtl_emmeans
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    trait_label =
      unname(
        trait_labels[
          trait
        ]
      )
  )

primary_qtl_emmeans
```

# 17. Overall Positive - Negative QTL contrasts

These are the overall adjusted QTL contrasts across backgrounds.

```{r overall-qtl-contrasts}
extract_overall_qtl_contrast <- function(
  result
) {

  if (
    inherits(
      result$model,
      "error"
    )
  ) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble()
    )
  }

  em <- emmeans::emmeans(
    result$model,
    ~ qtl_status
  )

  contrast_result <- emmeans::contrast(
    em,
    method = list(
      "Positive - Negative" =
        c(
          -1,
          1
        )
    ),
    adjust = "none"
  )

  as.data.frame(
    contrast_result
  ) |>
    janitor::clean_names() |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      trait = result$trait,
      .before = 1
    )
}

primary_overall_qtl_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(
  primary_model_results,
  extract_overall_qtl_contrast
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    trait_label =
      unname(
        trait_labels[
          trait
        ]
      ),
    fdr_p =
      stats::p.adjust(
        p_value,
        method = "BH"
      )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    fdr_p,
    p_value
  )

primary_overall_qtl_contrasts
```

# 18. Background-specific Positive - Negative contrasts

These contrasts describe the QTL effect within each background. They should be
interpreted together with the formal `Background × QTL` interaction rather than
using "significant in one background but not another" as evidence of interaction.

```{r background-specific-qtl-contrasts}
extract_background_qtl_contrasts <- function(
  result
) {

  if (
    inherits(
      result$model,
      "error"
    )
  ) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble()
    )
  }

  em <- emmeans::emmeans(
    result$model,
    ~ qtl_status | background
  )

  contrast_result <- emmeans::contrast(
    em,
    method = list(
      "Positive - Negative" =
        c(
          -1,
          1
        )
    ),
    by = "background",
    adjust = "none"
  )

  as.data.frame(
    contrast_result
  ) |>
    janitor::clean_names() |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      trait = result$trait,
      .before = 1
    )
}

primary_background_qtl_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(
  primary_model_results,
  extract_background_qtl_contrasts
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    trait_label =
      unname(
        trait_labels[
          trait
        ]
      )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    background
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fdr_p =
      stats::p.adjust(
        p_value,
        method = "BH"
      )
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

primary_background_qtl_contrasts
```

# 20. Primary model residual diagnostics

```{r primary-residual-diagnostics}
extract_primary_residuals <- function(
  result
) {

  if (
    inherits(
      result$model,
      "error"
    )
  ) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble()
    )
  }

  model_frame <- stats::model.frame(
    result$model
  )

  original_rows <- as.integer(
    rownames(
      model_frame
    )
  )

  diagnostic_data <- yarn_formal[
    original_rows,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  residual_values <- stats::residuals(
    result$model
  )

  residual_sd <- stats::sd(
    residual_values,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  diagnostic_data |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      trait = result$trait,
      field_sample_id,
      genotype,
      background,
      pair_id,
      qtl_status,
      field_rep,
      ratch,
      actual_yarn_count_ne,
      value =
        .data[[result$trait]],
      fitted_value =
        stats::fitted(
          result$model
        ),
      residual =
        residual_values,
      standardized_residual =
        residual_values /
        residual_sd
    )
}

primary_residuals <- purrr::map_dfr(
  primary_model_results,
  extract_primary_residuals
)

primary_residual_outliers <- primary_residuals |>
  dplyr::filter(
    abs(
      standardized_residual
    ) > 3
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    trait,
    dplyr::desc(
      abs(
        standardized_residual
      )
    )
  )

primary_diagnostic_summary <- primary_residuals |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    trait
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n =
      dplyr::n(),
    max_abs_standardized_residual =
      max(
        abs(
          standardized_residual
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    n_over_3sd =
      sum(
        abs(
          standardized_residual
        ) > 3,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

primary_diagnostic_summary
primary_residual_outliers
```

```{r save-primary-diagnostic-plots}
  ggplot2::ggsave(
```

# 25. Sensitivity analysis: adjustment for actual yarn count

Actual yarn count is not included in the primary model. This sensitivity analysis
asks whether QTL conclusions persist after adjusting for observed yarn linear
density.

The actual-yarn-count sensitivity is not fitted for `actual_yarn_count_ne` itself.

```{r yarn-count-sensitivity-function}
fit_count_adjusted_model <- function(
  trait
) {

  model_data <- yarn_formal |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(
        .data[[trait]]
      ),
      !is.na(
        actual_yarn_count_ne
      )
    ) |>
    droplevels()

  formula_object <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0(
      trait,
      " ~ background * qtl_status + field_rep + ",
      "actual_yarn_count_ne + (1 | pair_id)"
    )
  )

  fit <- tryCatch(
    lmerTest::lmer(
      formula_object,
      data = model_data,
      REML = TRUE,
      control =
        lme4::lmerControl(
          optimizer = "bobyqa",
          optCtrl = list(
            maxfun = 100000
          )
        )
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      e
    }
  )

  list(
    trait = trait,
    n = nrow(
      model_data
    ),
    model = fit
  )
}

count_adjusted_results <- purrr::map(
  primary_yarn_traits,
  fit_count_adjusted_model
)

names(

) <- primary_yarn_traits
```

# 29. Package-level confirmation models

Package-level confirmation preserves the two-package structure by adding a random
intercept for biological field sample. These models are secondary to the
sample-average analysis.

```{r package-level-confirmation}
package_traits <- c(
  "skein_mn_tex",
  "yarn_tenacity_cn_tex",
  "yarn_elongation_pct",
  "yarn_evenness_cv_pct",
  "yarn_thin_50",
  "yarn_thick_50",
  "yarn_neps_200",
  "yarn_hairiness"
)

fit_package_model <- function(
  trait
) {

  model_data <- package_formal |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(
        .data[[trait]]
      )
    ) |>
    droplevels()

  formula_object <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0(
      trait,
      " ~ background * qtl_status + field_rep + ",
      "(1 | pair_id) + (1 | field_sample_id)"
    )
  )

  fit <- tryCatch(
    lmerTest::lmer(
      formula_object,
      data = model_data,
      REML = TRUE,
      control =
        lme4::lmerControl(
          optimizer = "bobyqa",
          optCtrl = list(
            maxfun = 100000
          )
        )
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      e
    }
  )

  list(
    trait = trait,
    n = nrow(
      model_data
    ),
    model = fit
  )
}

package_model_results <- purrr::map(
  package_traits,
  fit_package_model
)

names(
  package_model_results
) <- package_traits

package_model_status <- purrr::map_dfr(
  package_model_results,
  function(result) {

    if (
      inherits(
        result$model,
        "error"
      )
    ) {
      return(
        tibble::tibble(
          trait = result$trait,
          n = result$n,
          fitted = FALSE,
          singular = NA,
          message =
            conditionMessage(
              result$model
            )
        )
      )
    }

    tibble::tibble(
      trait = result$trait,
      n = result$n,
      fitted = TRUE,
      singular =
        lme4::isSingular(
          result$model,
          tol = 1e-4
        ),
      message = NA_character_
    )
  }
)

package_qtl_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(

  extract_overall_qtl_contrast
) |>
```

# 30. Technical-replicate tensile-break QC

Individual breaks are summarized only to characterize within-package technical
variation. They are not treated as 3,680 independent biological observations.

```{r tensile-break-qc}
break_qc_by_package <- break_formal |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    field_sample_id,
    minispin_run,
    package,
    genotype,
    background,
    pair_id,
    qtl_status
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_breaks =
      dplyr::n(),
    mean_tenacity =
      mean(
        yarn_tenacity_cn_tex,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    sd_tenacity =
      stats::sd(
        yarn_tenacity_cn_tex,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    cv_tenacity_pct =
      100 *
      sd_tenacity /
      mean_tenacity,
    mean_break_force =
      mean(
        single_end_break_force_n,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    sd_break_force =
      stats::sd(
        single_end_break_force_n,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

break_qc_summary <- break_qc_by_package |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    packages =
      dplyr::n(),
    packages_with_20_breaks =
      sum(
        n_breaks == 20
      ),
    packages_not_20_breaks =
      sum(
        n_breaks != 20
      ),
    median_tenacity_cv_pct =
      stats::median(
        cv_tenacity_pct,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    max_tenacity_cv_pct =
      max(
        cv_tenacity_pct,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  )

break_qc_summary
```

# 31. Influence sensitivity excluding > |3 SD| primary residuals

This sensitivity removes only observations flagged by the corresponding primary
trait model. It is used to determine whether a QTL conclusion is driven by a small
number of influential observations; it does not automatically justify deleting
those observations from the primary analysis.

```{r outlier-sensitivity}
fit_outlier_sensitivity <- function(
  trait
) {

  flagged_ids <- primary_residual_outliers |>
    dplyr::filter(
      trait == !!trait
    ) |>
    dplyr::pull(
      field_sample_id
    ) |>
    as.character()

  model_data <- yarn_formal |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(
        .data[[trait]]
      ),
      !as.character(
        field_sample_id
      ) %in%
        flagged_ids
    ) |>
    droplevels()

  formula_object <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0(
      trait,
      " ~ background * qtl_status + field_rep + (1 | pair_id)"
    )
  )

  fit <- tryCatch(
    lmerTest::lmer(
      formula_object,
      data = model_data,
      REML = TRUE,
      control =
        lme4::lmerControl(
          optimizer = "bobyqa",
          optCtrl = list(
            maxfun = 100000
          )
        )
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      e
    }
  )

  list(
    trait = trait,
    n = nrow(
      model_data
    ),
    n_removed =
      length(
        unique(
          flagged_ids
        )
      ),
    model = fit
  )
}

outlier_sensitivity_results <- purrr::map(
  primary_yarn_traits,
  fit_outlier_sensitivity
)

names(
  outlier_sensitivity_results
) <- primary_yarn_traits

outlier_sensitivity_qtl <- purrr::map_dfr(
  outlier_sensitivity_results,
  function(result) {

    contrast_table <-
      extract_overall_qtl_contrast(
        result
      )

    if (
      nrow(
        contrast_table
      ) == 0
    ) {
      return(
        contrast_table
      )
    }

    contrast_table |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        n = result$n,
        n_removed =
          result$n_removed
      )
  }
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fdr_p =
      stats::p.adjust(
        p_value,
        method = "BH"
      )
  )

outlier_sensitivity_qtl
```

# 32. Overall QTL effect-size plot

```{r save-overall-qtl-effect-plot}
overall_effect_plot_data <- primary_overall_qtl_contrasts |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    lower =
      estimate -
      1.96 *
      se,
    upper =
      estimate +
      1.96 *
      se,
    trait_label =
      factor(
        trait_label,
        levels =
          rev(
            unname(
              trait_labels[
                primary_yarn_traits
              ]
            )
          )
      )
  )

p_overall_effect <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  overall_effect_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = trait_label
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbarh(
    ggplot2::aes(
      xmin = lower,
      xmax = upper
    ),
    height = 0.15
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = 2.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Overall qFL-Chr.25 effect on yarn traits",
    subtitle = "Positive - Negative estimated marginal mean",
    x = "Estimated QTL effect",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    yarn_figure_dir,
    "primary_yarn_overall_qtl_effects.png"
  ),
  plot = p_overall_effect,
  width = 9,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 300
)

p_overall_effect
```

# 33. Save primary models

```{r save-models}
purrr::iwalk(
  primary_model_results,
  function(result, trait_name) {

    if (
      !inherits(
        result$model,
        "error"
      )
    ) {
      saveRDS(
        result$model,
        file.path(
          yarn_model_dir,
          paste0(
            "primary_",
            trait_name,
            "_model.rds"
          )
        )
      )
    }
  }
)
```

# 35. Final analysis audit

```{r final-analysis-audit}
primary_failed <-
  sum(
    !primary_model_status$fitted
  )

primary_singular <-
  sum(
    primary_model_status$singular,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

primary_qtl_fdr_significant <-
  primary_overall_qtl_contrasts |>
  dplyr::filter(
    fdr_p < 0.05
  ) |>
  nrow()

primary_bgqtl_fdr_significant <-
  primary_type3_tests |>
  dplyr::filter(
    effect ==
      "background:qtl_status",
    fdr_p < 0.05
  ) |>
  nrow()

final_analysis_audit <- tibble::tibble(
  check = c(
    "Formal NIIL samples",
    "Primary yarn traits requested",
    "Primary models fitted",
    "Primary models failed",
    "Primary singular models",
    "Primary overall QTL contrasts",
    "Primary QTL contrasts FDR < 0.05",
    "Background × QTL tests FDR < 0.05",
    "Primary residual observations > |3 SD|",
    "Package-level confirmation models",
    "Technical-break rows"
  ),
  result = c(
    nrow(
      yarn_formal
    ),
    length(
      primary_yarn_traits
    ),
    sum(
      primary_model_status$fitted
    ),
    primary_failed,
    primary_singular,
    nrow(
      primary_overall_qtl_contrasts
    ),
    primary_qtl_fdr_significant,
    primary_bgqtl_fdr_significant,
    nrow(
      primary_residual_outliers
    ),
    sum(
      package_model_status$fitted
    ),
    nrow(
      break_formal
    )
  )
)

final_analysis_audit

readr::write_csv(
  final_analysis_audit,
  file.path(
    yarn_table_dir,
    "yarn_final_analysis_audit.csv"
  ),
  na = ""
)
```
